title: Risk of Large-Scale War Rising — UN Report
paragraphs: What's the biggest threat facing the world today? This is what the United Nations (UN) asked 1,300 experts around the world. And while climate change has been seen as our biggest threat for some time, the risk of large-scale war is rising.

In 2024, the first UN Global Risk Report assessed what global risks needed action. At the time, the top risks were climate change inaction, large-scale pollution, misinformation and natural hazards like fires, droughts and heat waves.
For the 2026 report, the UN again called on experts and decision makers from global governments, businesses and civil society organizations, as well as experts in the UN itself.

They were given a list of 28 global risks and asked to assess how likely each one is to occur, how serious its effects could be, how soon it might happen and how prepared international organizations are to respond.

The top perceived threat is still climate change inaction. However, it's also the risk for which we're best prepared. Misinformation is also still seen as a big threat — and one for which we're much less prepared.
However, over the past two years, the perceived risk of large-scale pollution has decreased significantly — while the danger of large-scale war has exploded.

Large-scale war moved up 16 places from the 2024 rankings — the largest jump on the list. And 36% of those surveyed said they expect a large-scale war within a year, while 76% expect it within seven years. It's also one of the risks for which we're least prepared.
Similarly, AI is now perceived as a much greater threat than it was in 2024 — and we're even less prepared for the dangers of AI than we are for a large-scale war.
Respondents said that, globally, we need a better shared understanding of emerging risks, while a lack of funding is hampering our response to well-known dangers.

However, many agree that the most effective response is for governments to work together. UN Secretary General António Guterres said, "No country, no company, no institution can face these risks alone."
